learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods, and to correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and use databases and other sources of information critically, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the engineering field and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.
Ability to stay up-to-date with new developments in science and technology.
Describe the anatomy and understand the general physiology of the different systems of the human body, being able to identify and know the different elements that constitute these systems.
Understand the function of cellular organelles, differentiate different types of cells, and characterize the different types of tissues.

syllabus_topics: Anatomy and physiology of the locomotor system
Anatomy and physiology of the respiratory system
Anatomy and physiology of the heart
teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams, and/or control points
Teacher presentation in class, in participatory sessions, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Workshops, debates, seminars, case studies, role-playing games, etc.
Practices in workshops and/or laboratories, individually or in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, presentation and technical defense
Individual written, coding/programming, and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For one part of the course (associated with RAB02 outcomes), assessment includes individual written and oral tests (20%), technical capacity, project involvement, work, results, documentation, presentation, and technical defense (30%), and individual written, coding/programming, and oral tests for technical competencies (50%). No recovery mechanisms are specified for this part. For another part (associated with RAB01 outcomes), assessment includes individual written and oral tests for technical competencies (80%) and reports on exercises, case studies, computer, simulation, and laboratory practices (20%). Recovery for this part involves written and oral individual tests for technical competencies. The syllabus does not provide a single grading formula to combine these two parts into a final course grade.
